sense: at the time that (not the question)

terms.grammar: conjunction: the indicative for the time pure and simple (present, future, and things that happen again and again); in past narrative the imperfect or pluperfect subjunctive
evidence: Ter. And. 309: Facile omnēs, cum valēmus, rēcta cōnsilia aegrōtīs damus.
Quint. 1.9.5: cum indoctum puerum vīdisset, paedagōgum ejus percussit
terms.comment: “When he had seen …” in a story is cum vīdisset; “when you come” is the future perfect, cum vēneris, as after sī (see if).

terms.grammar: conjunction, with the indicative (perfect in narrative)
evidence: Cic. Rep. 6.14: quem ubi vīdī, equidem vim lacrimārum prōfūdī (Lewis & Short)
Phaedr. 1.30.1: humilēs labōrant ubi potentēs dissident
Cic. Att. 5.1.3: ut vēnī in Arpīnās

phrases.latin: Facile omnēs, cum valēmus, rēcta cōnsilia aegrōtīs damus.
phrases.english: When we are well, we all find it easy to give good advice to the sick.

phrases.latin: istō bonō ūtāre, dum adsit; cum absit, nē requīrās
phrases.english: make use of that good while you have it; when it is gone, do not pine for it

phrases.latin: ut Cratēs, cum indoctum puerum vīdisset, paedagōgum ejus percussit
phrases.english: as Crates, when he had seen an ignorant boy, struck the boy’s tutor

phrases.latin: quem ubi vīdī, equidem vim lacrimārum prōfūdī
phrases.english: when I saw him, I burst into tears

phrases.latin: ut vēnī in Arpīnās, cum ad mē frāter vēnisset, in prīmīs nōbīs sermō isque multus dē tē fuit
phrases.english: when I arrived at Arpinum and my brother had come to me, our first talk, and a long one, was about you
